newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters strike Alliant Techsystems unit.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters strike Alliant Techsystems unit.

text.p: HOPKINS, Minn. - About 474 members of Teamsters Local 1145 struck two Minnesota facilities of Alliant Techsystems at midnight Sunday over outsourcing provisions in the final contract offer made by Alliant on Saturday, the union said.
The defense contractor based here and the union had been negotiating a new three year contract, with the old contract having been extended since it expired one week ago.
Alliant spokesman Rod Bitz told Reuters that of the $1.7 billion in pending contract work, about $25 million to $30 million is performed at the two Minnesota facilities affected by the strike.
The workers are members of Alliant's Defense Systems Group.

The secretary-treasurer for the Teamsters local, Bill Tyler, told Reuters that the union would have voted for the contract if it had not been for provisions which would alter Alliant's ability to outsource work.

"We could have got it passed on the things they put up front," Tyler said, "but on the last page of the offer they want to throw out our protections on subcontracting. They want to be able to subcontract out any job, any time, anywhere."

But Bitz said some limits would remain. "While there would be fewer restrictions on the company's ability to outsource," Bitz said, "the union will still continue to bid for the work, and disputes will still be handled through arbitration."
Bitz and Tyler confirmed that Alliant's offer included a three percent wage increase in each of the contract's three years and a 15 percent increase in pension benefits.
Asked if the company would hire replacement workers, Bitz said, "We'd really like to resolve this before we'd consider anything like that."
